items.title: Edge case tally: what the wizard skills stamp out that a generic agent gets wrong
items.body:
Running tally of edge cases a generic agent gets wrong when adding PostHog, and the shape the wizard skills and harness produce instead. In each block `-` is the generic agent and `+` is the wizard. The list continues in the comments below.

Adding PostHog looks like a five-line job, but most of the ways it goes wrong raise no error, so a generic agent ships broken analytics and reports success. This tally lists 944 such failures, each seen in a real wizard run, benchmark, PR or issue over the past year and turned into a context-mill skill rule or a wizard harness check. The skills are long because each rule holds back one of these failures, and many rules exist because the first fix went too far.

**Why generic runs fail:** failures are silent, so the agent cannot self-correct; docs, examples and training data are wrong or stale; each framework has its own lifecycle and wiring; the obvious fix over-corrects; verification signals lie; steps undo each other unless ordered; the harness enforces what prompts cannot; generic agents damage code outside the integration; helpful defaults leak personal data and secrets.

**Contents:** Still unfixed (18, see the [remarks comment](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/issues/1439#issuecomment-6131235777)) · Events dropped at process exit (28) · Content Security Policy blocks the SDK (10) · Users not identified or reset (26) · Wrong or shared person ids (28) · Success reported without proof (74) · Missing or misnamed config (42) · Personal data sent to PostHog (26) · Secrets leaked or untrusted input followed (59) · SDK started in the wrong place (23) · Framework-specific wiring missed (100) · SDK APIs used wrongly (69) · Wrong PostHog region or host (11) · Reverse proxy missing or broken (13) · Errors not captured or unreadable (86) · Events that mislead analysis (43) · Feature flags read wrongly (36) · Packages installed wrongly (46) · Changes that break builds or deploys (3) · Edits beyond the integration (55) · Dashboard and PostHog tool calls fail (68) · Wizard run mechanics (98)

## Events dropped at process exit

**Server route returns before batched event sends** [cm#228](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/228) [cm#212](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/212)
Silent: on serverless or edge the function freezes on return before the batched HTTP send, so server events are dropped. Low-traffic endpoints lose most events.
```diff
- // lib/posthog-server.ts
- const posthog = new PostHog(token, { host })   // default batching: 20 events / 10s
- export async function POST(request: Request) {
-   posthog.capture({ distinctId: username, event: 'server_login' })
-   return NextResponse.json({ success: true, user }) // returns before the send
- }
+ // lib/posthog-server.ts
+ new PostHog(token, { host, flushAt: 1, flushInterval: 0 })
+ // api/auth/login/route.ts
+ posthog.capture({ distinctId: username, event: 'server_login' })
+ // This handler is short-lived; flush so the enqueued events send before it returns
+ await posthog.flush()
```

**Server error hook captures but never flushes** [cm#228](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/228) [workbench#2009](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/2009)
Silent: the one event that describes the failure is the one most likely to be lost.
```diff
- export const handleError: HandleServerError = async ({ error, status, message }) => {
-   posthog.capture({ distinctId: 'server', event: 'server_error',
-     properties: { error: String(error), status, message } })  // batched, never sent
-   return { message, status }
- }
+ // singleton: new PostHog(token, { host, flushAt: 1, flushInterval: 0 })
+ export const handleError: HandleServerError = async ({ error, status, message }) => {
+   posthog.capture({ distinctId: 'server', event: 'server_error',
+     properties: { error: String(error), status, message } })
+   // handleError runs per request; flush so the event sends before it returns
+   await posthog.flush()
```

**Shutting down the shared client every request** [workbench#2712](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/2712) [cm#228](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/228)
Silent: after the first request the cached client is terminated and its flush timer cleared, so every later request drops its events; overlapping calls log warnings.
```diff
- const posthog = getPostHogServer()   // module-level singleton
- posthog.capture({ distinctId, event: 'contact_form_received' })
- await posthog.shutdown()             // every request, closes the shared client
+ const posthog = getPostHogClient()   // flushAt: 1, flushInterval: 0
+ posthog.capture({ distinctId, event: 'server_login' })
+ await posthog.flush()      // shared client: flush per request, client stays alive
+ // shutdown() only for a per-request client, or once at process exit
```

**Per-request server client never shut down** [cm#228](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/228)
Silent: the batch never sends before the handler ends, so events like server_login are lost, and every request leaks a client with its timers and sockets.
```diff
- export async function action({ request }: Route.ActionArgs) {
-   const posthog = new PostHog(process.env.POSTHOG_KEY!, { host })
-   posthog.capture({ distinctId: username, event: 'server_login' })
-   return Response.json({ success: true })   // never shut down
- }
+ export const posthogMiddleware: Route.MiddlewareFunction = async ({ request, context }, next) => {
+   const posthog = new PostHog(token, { host, flushAt: 1, flushInterval: 0 })
+   ;(context as PostHogContext).posthog = posthog
+   const response = await posthog.withContext({ sessionId, distinctId }, next)
+   await posthog.shutdown().catch(() => {}) // per-request client: shutdown, not flush
+   return response
```

**Node server has no shutdown on SIGTERM** [wizard#1330](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/issues/1330) [wizard#283](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/283)
Silent: events and OTel log records still queued at every stop, deploy or restart are lost.
```diff
- const posthog = new PostHog(token, { host })
- app.post('/todos', (req, res) => {
-   posthog.capture({ distinctId: id, event: 'todo_added' })
-   res.status(201).json(todo)
- })
- app.listen(PORT) // no SIGINT/SIGTERM handler, nothing calls posthog.shutdown()
+ const server = app.listen(PORT)
+ async function shutdown() {
+   server.close()
+   await posthog.shutdown() // drains the batch
+   process.exit(0)
+ }
```

**Minimality review deletes the shutdown helper** [wizard#1330](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/issues/1330) [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245)
The run's only shutdown path is removed, so buffered events and logs are lost at exit.
```diff
- - let sdk;
- - async function shutdownLogs() { await sdk?.shutdown() }
- // log: 'The minimality review found one unused exported shutdown helper; removing it'
+ // shutdown/flush wiring is never an 'unused helper': wire it, don't delete it
+ process.on('SIGTERM', async () => {
+   server.close();
+   await posthog.shutdown();
+ });
```

**Node script exits before the batch sends** [cm#108](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/108) [cm#228](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/228)
Silent: pending events are dropped at exit.
```diff
- const posthog = new PostHog(key, { host })
- posthog.capture({ distinctId: 'cli', event: 'job_done' })
- process.exit(0) // batched HTTP send never ran
+ const posthog = new PostHog(key, { host })
+ posthog.capture({ distinctId: 'cli', event: 'job_done' })
+ await posthog.shutdown()   // short-lived process: flush and close
+ process.exit(0)
+ // long-lived shared client: await posthog.flush() instead
```

**Python script exits without calling shutdown** [cm#70](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/70) [cm#108](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/108)
Silent: events still in the in-memory queue are often lost when the process exits, especially for a short CLI run.
```diff
- posthog_client = Posthog(token, host=host)
- def main():
-     posthog_client.capture('job_finished', distinct_id=user_id)
-     sys.exit(0)  # queue never flushed
+ posthog_client = Posthog(token, host=host, enable_exception_autocapture=True)
+ atexit.register(posthog_client.shutdown)  # commandment, not in todo.py
+ try:
+     run_command(args, posthog_client)
+ finally:
+     # IMPORTANT: Always shutdown PostHog to flush events
```

**FastAPI app has no shutdown flush** [cm#63](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/63) [wizard#251](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/251)
Silent: events still queued when uvicorn stops or reloads are lost, and config errors show up at import time instead of startup.
```diff
- import posthog
- posthog.api_key = settings.posthog_project_token   # runs at import
- posthog.host = settings.posthog_host
- app = FastAPI()   # no lifespan, nothing flushes on shutdown
+ @asynccontextmanager
+ async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
+     if not settings.posthog_disabled:
+         posthog.api_key = settings.posthog_project_token
+         posthog.host = settings.posthog_host
+     yield
```

**Laravel queue job events never sent** [cm#282](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/282)
Silent: job events sit in memory for hours and are lost on worker restart.
```diff
- class TriageFeedback implements ShouldQueue {
-     public function handle(): void {
-         PostHog::capture([
-             'distinctId' => (string) $this->user->id,
-             'event' => 'feedback_triage_completed',
-         ]); // buffered, never sent
+ public function handle(): void {
+     PostHog::capture([
+         'distinctId' => (string) $this->user->id,
+         'event' => 'feedback_triage_completed',
+     ]);
+     PostHog::flush(); // long-running worker never destructs
```

**PHP script or WordPress hook never flushes** [cm#279](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/279) [cm#136](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/136)
Silent: buffered events are lost in CLIs, cron jobs and WordPress hooks.
```diff
- add_action('comment_post', function ($id, $approved, $data) {
-     PostHog::capture([
-         'distinctId' => (string) $data['user_id'],
-         'event' => 'comment_posted',
-     ]);
- }, 10, 3);
+ PostHog::capture([
+     'distinctId' => (string) $distinct_id,
+     'event' => 'comment_posted',
+     'properties' => ['comment_id' => $comment_id],
+ ]);
+ PostHog::flush(); // no single exit point in a web request
```

**Lambda and job worker captures never flushed** [cm#228](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/228) [cm#193](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/193)
Silent: events captured just before the process or invocation ends are lost. One customer lost a measurable share of subscription events in Celery workers.
```diff
- export async function handler(event) {
-   posthog.capture({ distinctId: id, event: 'order_paid' })
-   return { statusCode: 200 }
- }
+ const posthog = new PostHog(key, { host, flushAt: 1, flushInterval: 0 })
+ export async function handler(event) {
+   posthog.capture({ distinctId: id, event: 'order_paid' })
+   await posthog.flush()   // shared client; shutdown() only for a per-request client
+   return { statusCode: 200 }
+ }
```

**Rust app with no shutdown hook skips flush** [cm#354](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/354) [cm#353](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/353)
Silent: captures still queued when main returns are never delivered.
```diff
- let client = posthog_rs::client(options).await;
- client.capture(Event::new("file_served", &id)).await?;
- // no graceful-shutdown hook, so no flush/shutdown added
- axum::serve(listener, app).await?;
+ axum::serve(listener, app)
+     .with_graceful_shutdown(shutdown_signal())
+     .await
+     .expect("server error");
+ // capture is fire-and-forget: flush, then stop the worker
+ client.flush().await;
```

**Go client never closed on shutdown** [cm#153](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/153) [cm#267](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/267)
Silent: events still queued at SIGTERM or exit are dropped.
```diff
- func main() {
- 	client, _ := posthog.NewWithConfig(token, posthog.Config{Endpoint: host})
- 	a := &app{posthog: client}
- 	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8000", a.routes())) // queue never drained
- }
+ srv := &http.Server{Addr: ":8000", Handler: a.routes()}
+ go srv.ListenAndServe()
+ <-stop // SIGINT/SIGTERM
+ srv.Shutdown(ctx)
+ client.Close() // blocks until the queue drains
```

**Go log.Fatal skips the deferred Close** [cm#267](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/267)
Silent: the queued batch is dropped on every restart.
```diff
- client := posthog.New(token)
- defer client.Close() // skipped: log.Fatal calls os.Exit
- log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8000", mux))
+ stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
+ signal.Notify(stop, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
+ <-stop
+ srv.Shutdown(ctx)
+ if err := client.Close(); err != nil { // blocks until the queue drains
+     log.Printf("error closing PostHog client: %v", err)
```

**Java client never closed when the JVM stops** [cm#270](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/270) [wizard#948](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/948)
Silent: the batch queue is not flushed when the Spring context or JVM stops, or clients multiply per request.
```diff
- @GetMapping("/x")
- String x() {
-     PostHogInterface posthog = PostHog.with(
-         PostHogConfig.builder(token).host(host).build()); // per request, never closed
-     posthog.capture(userId, "x_viewed");
-     return "x";
+ @Bean(destroyMethod = "close")
+ public PostHogInterface posthog(
+         @Value("${posthog.project-token:}") String projectToken,
+         @Value("${posthog.host:https://us.i.posthog.com}") String host) {
+     return PostHog.with(PostHogConfig.builder(projectToken).host(host).build());
+ }
```

**.NET CLI exits without FlushAsync** [cm#145](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/145)
Silent: queued events are never sent from short-lived .NET processes.
```diff
- var posthog = new PostHogClient(options);
- posthog.Capture(userId, "report_generated");
- return 0; // exits with events still queued
+ var posthog = new PostHogClient(options); // one client per process
+ posthog.Capture(userId, "report_generated");
+ await posthog.FlushAsync();               // before exit
+ return 0;
```

**Ruby script skips shutdown on some exit paths** [cm#85](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/85) [wizard#276](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/276)
Silent: buffered events from a short-lived Ruby process are lost and nothing raises.
```diff
- posthog = PostHog::Client.new(api_key: ENV['POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN'])
- posthog.capture(distinct_id: id, event: 'todo_added')
- exit 1 unless ok   # no shutdown on this path
- # script ends; queue never flushed
+ begin
+   posthog = initialize_posthog
+   run_cli(ARGV, posthog)
+ rescue StandardError => e
+   posthog&.capture_exception(e, get_user_id)
+   exit 1
```

**Metrics lost when a short script exits** [cm#342](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/342) [cm#255](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/255)
Silent: no metrics arrive at all.
```diff
- posthog.metrics.count("job.processed")
- posthog.metrics.histogram("job.duration", ms, unit="ms")
- sys.exit(0)   # exits before the flush interval
+ posthog.metrics.count("job.processed")
+ posthog.metrics.histogram("job.duration", ms, unit="ms")
+ # short-lived processes (scripts, cron, serverless): flush before exit
+ posthog.metrics.flush()          # or shutdown()
+ # OTel path: provider.force_flush() / shutdown()
```

**Trace spans lost when the process exits** [cm#373](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/373) [cm#391](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/391)
Silent: buffered spans are lost; serverless handlers and scripts send nothing.
```diff
- tp := sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(sdktrace.WithSpanProcessor(posthogProcessor))
- otel.SetTracerProvider(tp)
- // main returns, no ForceFlush / Shutdown
+ tp := sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(sdktrace.WithSpanProcessor(posthogProcessor))
+ otel.SetTracerProvider(tp)
+ defer func() { _ = tp.Shutdown(ctx) }() // or tp.ForceFlush(ctx) before exit
+ // serverless handler: ForceFlush at the end of each invocation, Shutdown only on process exit
```

**LLM script exits before AI events flush** [cm#319](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/319) [workbench#3358](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/3358)
Silent: the run completes with no error but no $ai_generation events ever arrive.
```diff
- def main():
-     reply = client.chat.completions.create(model='gpt-5-mini', messages=messages)
-     print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
- # process exits here, queued events are lost
+ reply = client.chat.completions.create(model='gpt-5-mini', messages=messages)
+ print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
+ posthog.shutdown()  # flush queued events before a short script exits
+ # OTel path: tracer_provider.force_flush() / shutdown() before exit
```

**Serverless MCP server relies on a SIGTERM flush** [cm#202](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/202)
Silent: batched $mcp_* tool-call events are lost at the end of each invocation.
```diff
- const handler = createMcpHandler((server) => {
-   instrument(server, posthog)
- })
- process.on('SIGTERM', async () => { await posthog.shutdown() }) // never runs here
+ // serverless / edge: flush at the end of each invocation
+ await posthog.flush()
+ // or, where supported:
+ ctx.waitUntil(posthog.flush())
+ // long-running STDIO / persistent HTTP: await posthog.shutdown() on SIGTERM
```

**Python MCP server exits without draining analytics** [cm#205](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/205)
Silent: in-flight auto-captured MCP events are dropped when the process exits.
```diff
- analytics = instrument(server, posthog)
- server.run()
- # exit: no await analytics.flush(), no posthog.shutdown()
+ # long-running server (STDIO or persistent HTTP): drain on exit
+ await analytics.flush()   # waits for in-flight auto-capture events
+ posthog.shutdown()        # flushes and stops the client
```

**Cloudflare Worker ends before the batch sends** [wizard#370](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/370) [wizard#385](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/385)
Silent: the isolate terminates before the async batched send runs, and env values read at module scope may be undefined.
```diff
- const posthog = new PostHog(process.env.POSTHOG_KEY, { host }) // module scope, batching
- export default {
-   async fetch(request, env, ctx) {
-     posthog.capture({ distinctId, event: 'hello' })
-     return new Response('ok') // isolate may end first
-   },
+ const posthog = new PostHog(env.POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN, {
+   host: env.POSTHOG_HOST, flushAt: 1, flushInterval: 0,
+ }) // new client per request, inside fetch
+ ctx.waitUntil(posthog.captureImmediate({ distinctId, event: 'hello_world_request' }))
+ ctx.waitUntil(posthog.shutdown())
+ return new Response('ok')
```

**Logout event lost to full-page form submit** [wizard#1121](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/issues/1121)
Silent: the logout capture can be lost in the unload, and reset() competes with the pending flush.
```diff
- <form action="/auth/logout" method="post"
-   onSubmit={() => { posthog.capture('user_logged_out'); posthog.reset() }}>
+ // intended shape, no ordering rule yet (issue 1121 item 5 open):
+ // send the capture so it survives navigation, then reset()
+ posthog.capture('user_logged_out', {}, { transport: 'sendBeacon' })
+ posthog.reset()
```

**Migration maps Statsig shutdown to PostHog everywhere** [cm#142](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/142) [wizard#474](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/474)
Runtime errors or dead calls in the browser, and real server teardown handlers handled wrongly.
```diff
- // browser code
- - statsig.shutdown()
- + posthog.shutdown()
- - statsig.flush()
- + posthog.flush()   // no client-side equivalent
+ // statsig.shutdown(): ambiguous
+ //   client side: usually no PostHog teardown needed
+ //   clear server teardown handler: posthog.shutdown() (Node)
+ // statsig.flush() -> posthog.flush() server side only
+ // otherwise mark the site `warning`
```

**CLI exits on Ctrl+C or closed terminal before analytics flush** [wizard#873](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/873) [wizard#1416](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/1416)
Silent: interrupted runs vanish from the funnel. #873 saw about 470 warehouse agent starts but fewer than 100 terminal events; #1417 saw 12-20% of integrate runs since 2.75.0 send only 'wizard: started'.
```diff
- void waitUntilExit().then(() => {
-   cleanup()
-   process.exit(process.exitCode ?? 0) // analytics.shutdown() never runs
- })
- // no SIGHUP handler
+ const stop = (code: number) => {
+   unmountTui()
+   void (async () => {
+     try { await analytics.shutdown('cancelled') } catch { /* never block the end */ }
+     exit.end(code)
+   })()
```

**Wrong waitUntil source per framework on Workers** [cm#104](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/104)
ctx or runtime is undefined, so the request throws or the flush is skipped and events are lost.
```diff
- // src/pages/api/track.ts (Astro 6 on Workers)
- export const POST = async ({ locals }) => {
-   const posthog = createPostHogClient(locals.runtime.env) // runtime removed in Astro 6
-   locals.runtime.ctx.waitUntil(posthog.shutdown())
-   return new Response('ok')
- }
+ import { env, waitUntil } from 'cloudflare:workers'
+ export const POST = async () => {
+   const posthog = createPostHogClient(env)
+   // framework-agnostic; Astro 6 also exposes locals.cfContext.waitUntil
+   waitUntil(posthog.shutdown())
+   return new Response('ok')
```

## Content Security Policy blocks the SDK

**Review trusts 'CSP handled' without checking directives** [cm#278](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/278)
A partial CSP passes review, so replay, surveys and the toolbar silently never load (events still send, so the integration looks alive).
```diff
- init handoff: "Content-Security-Policy handled."
- review: reads handoff, marks CSP dimension done
-         (never opens the policy to check script-src / connect-src / worker-src)
+ # init handoff names directives touched and left alone:
+ #   touched script-src, connect-src, worker-src; left X alone
+ # (an unnamed directive reads as unhandled, not as fine)
+ # review verifies directive-by-directive, not on the handoff's word:
+ script-src  allows PostHog hosts (needed even when posthog-js is bundled;
+             replay/surveys/toolbar lazy-load from the assets CDN)
```

**Site CSP blocks the SDK, zero events** [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245) [cm#278](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/278)
Silent: the diff looks complete and zero events ever arrive.
```diff
- <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'">
- <script>
-   !function(t,e){/* loads us-assets.i.posthog.com/static/array.js */}(document,window.posthog||[]);
-   posthog.init(apiKey, { api_host: 'https://us.i.posthog.com' })
- </script>
+ # extend the existing policy, every directive in one pass
+ script-src:  https://*.posthog.com   (lazy-loaded bundles, even when self-hosting the entry)

- // next-auth: getServerSession(req, res) without authOptions -> session.user.id undefined
+ // Prove the id reaches the line; expose it at the source if missing
+ public function share(Request $request): array
+ {
+     return array_merge(parent::share($request), [
+         'auth' => ['user' => $request->user()?->only('id', 'email', 'name')],
+     ]);
```

**Coerced missing id becomes the string undefined** [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245)
Every user is identified as 'undefined' (or '') and pooled onto one person; silent.
```diff
- onSuccess: (page) => {
-   const user = page.props.auth?.user
-   if (user) posthog.identify(String(user.id))   // user exists, id absent -> 'undefined'
- }
+ // never pass a value that can be undefined; never substitute an email
+ if (!user?.id) return
+ posthog.identify(user.id, { email: user.email })
```

**PHP cast before ?? yields an empty id** [cm#101](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/101)
Events and exceptions are captured with an empty distinct id; silent.
```diff
- $distinctId = $distinctId
-     ?? (string) Auth::user()?->id
-     ?? 'anonymous'; // (string) null === "", never reaches here
+ $userId = Auth::user()?->id;
+ $distinctId = $distinctId
+     ?? ($userId !== null ? (string) $userId : null);
+ // no user: skip person attribution, never a shared literal
```

**Literal anonymous fallback pools all users** [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245) [cm#108](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/108)
Silent: every logged-out visitor or unattributed server event lands on one giant person, corrupting counts, funnels, retention and person merges.
```diff
- signIn: async ({ user, account }) => {
-   const distinctId = user?.id ?? user?.email ?? "anonymous";
-   posthog.identify({ distinctId, properties: { name: user?.name, email: user?.email } });
-   posthog.capture({ distinctId, event: "server_sign_in" });
- }
- // go
+ callbacks: {
+   session({ session, token }) {
+     if (session.user && typeof token.sub === "string") session.user.id = token.sub;
+     return session;
+   },
+ },
```

**Visible placeholder when no stable id reaches** [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245)
Events attach to the wrong person or nobody, and the user cannot find which call sites to fix.
```diff
- posthog.capture({
-   distinctId: user?.email ?? 'unknown',
-   event: 'export_started',
- });
- // report: "Note: some events may not be fully attributed to users."
+ // identity exists, no stable id reaches this call site
+ posthog.capture({ distinctId: 'DISTINCT_ID', event: 'invoice_paid' });
+ // report, own issue:
+ // Replace DISTINCT_ID in src/jobs/billing.ts:42, src/jobs/mail.ts:17
+ // Cost if left alone: those events belong to nobody.
```

**Accountless apps get personless events, not fake ids** [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245)
Silent: every visitor collapses into one made-up person, identification is claimed that does not exist, or a placeholder ships to production.
```diff
- // app has no accounts or login
- posthog.identify('user')                                   // invented
- posthog.capture({ distinctId: 'anonymous', event: 'newsletter_subscribed' })
- // or a placeholder shipped to production
- posthog.capture({ distinctId: 'DISTINCT_ID', event: 'file_uploaded' })
+ // App has no accounts: identify says so and stops; capture is personless
+ posthog.capture({ distinctId: randomUUID(), event: 'newsletter_subscribed',
+   properties: { $process_person_profile: false } })
+ // handoff: events are personless because the app has no identity
+ // DISTINCT_ID placeholder only when identity exists but no stable id reaches the call site
```

**Example READMEs still teach email ids** [cm#101](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/101)
The agent may pick the README shape and ship PII distinct ids; silent.
```diff
- // example-apps/laravel/README.md (ships into references/EXAMPLE.md)
- $posthog->identify($user->email, $user->getPostHogProperties());
- $posthog->capture($user->email, 'user_logged_in');
- # example-apps/fastapi/README.md
- identify_context(user.email)
+ # the code in the same Python examples
+ identify_context(str(user.id))          # fastapi app/middleware.py, routers/main.py
+ identify_context(str(current_user.id))  # flask app/api/routes.py
```

**Per-login or per-session id passed to identify** [workbench#4430](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/4430) [workbench#772](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/772)
Every login, session or device creates a new person, so retention, per-user funnels and cross-device counts break; silent.
```diff
- // mock auth: credentials.id = crypto.randomUUID() on each login
- this.posthogService.posthog.identify(credentials.id, {
-   username: credentials.username,
-   email: credentials.email,
- })
- // also: posthog.identify(session.sessionId), posthog.identify(req.cookies.sid)
+ // stable app id (primary key, uuid, resource name), never regenerated per login
+ posthog.identify(stableUserId, { username, email })
+ // audit: error when the id sources from a session, request or device id that resets
```

**Agent adds a schema migration to get an id** [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245)
Unrequested migration in the user's app for an analytics task; review burden and risk.
```diff
- -- migration added by the agent (lunalytics round 2)
- ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN userId TEXT;
- -- then: posthog.identify(user.userId)
+ The distinct id is the app's own stable identifier for the user - a primary key,
+ a uuid, a resource name. Not an email and not a username: those are PII and they
+ change; send them as person properties instead. Fall back to email only when the
+ app truly has no other stable key, and say so in your handoff - do not invent one
+ by altering the app's schema.
```

**Hand-rolled session header instead of tracing_headers** [cm#265](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/265) [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245)
Silent: only the session id travels, so server events join the browser session but split off into a different person.
```diff
- const sessionId = window.posthog?.get_session_id?.() || null
- await fetch('/api/events/burrito', { method: 'POST',
-   headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-PostHog-Session-Id': sessionId || '' } })
+ posthog.init(apiKey, { api_host: apiHost, defaults: '2026-01-30',
+   tracing_headers: [window.location.hostname] })
+ await fetch('/api/events/burrito', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } })
+ // SDK adds X-POSTHOG-SESSION-ID and X-POSTHOG-DISTINCT-ID itself
```

**Server events use a different id than the browser** [cm#265](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/265) [cm#67](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/67)
Silent: one user becomes two persons and server events are missing from the browser session and its replay.
```diff
- // client identifies with user.id
- fetch('/api/checkout', { method: 'POST' })
- // server
- posthog.capture({ distinctId: crypto.randomUUID(), event: 'checkout_completed' })
- // or distinctId: username / req.ip / user.email / a body field
+ // browser: init with tracing_headers: ['api.example.com'] adds both headers
+ // middleware: bind the browser's ids once per request
+ const sessionId = request.headers.get('X-POSTHOG-SESSION-ID')
+ const distinctId = request.headers.get('X-POSTHOG-DISTINCT-ID')
+ return posthog.withContext(
+   { sessionId: sessionId ?? undefined, distinctId: distinctId ?? undefined }, next)
```

**Form API route keys events on submitted email** [workbench#1120](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/1120) [workbench#4451](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/4451)
Server events fragment across emails or pool onto one person, never join the browser person, and with no distinctId the capture fails.
```diff
- posthog.capture({
-   distinctId: distinctId || data.email || 'anonymous',
-   event: 'contact_form_received',
-   properties: { name: data.name },
- })
+ const distinctId = request.headers.get('X-POSTHOG-DISTINCT-ID') ?? undefined;
+ const sessionId = request.headers.get('X-POSTHOG-SESSION-ID') ?? undefined;
+ // ids come from the browser's tracing_headers; never email, 'anonymous' or a random UUID
+ posthog.withContext({ distinctId, sessionId }, () =>
+   posthog.capture({ event: 'contact_form_received', properties: { source: 'api' } }))
```

**Capture instrumented before identity is settled** [cm#245](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/245) [cm#27](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/issues/27)
Silent: some events are double-wrapped, others personless or under a guessed id, depending on ordering.
```diff
- # seed graph before
- identify  dependsOn: [install, init]
- capture   dependsOn: [install, init]   # races identify
- # capture writes bare calls or its own identify_context per call
+ # capture.md frontmatter
+ dependsOn: [install, init, identify]
+ # read the identify handoff first: identity established -> plain capture;
+ # not established -> tag the call with distinct id and session id;
+ # identity exists but no id reaches -> DISTINCT_ID placeholder and say so
```

**Audit wrongly demands identify() on server SDKs** [cm#129](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/129)
False findings push agents to add pointless server identify calls while literal 'server' ids that pool all events go unflagged.
```diff
- client.capture({ distinctId: 'server', event: 'invoice_paid' })
- // auditor: "FAIL: no identify() call found on server"
+ client.capture({ distinctId: user.id, event: 'invoice_paid' })
+ // server SDKs identify per call: pass if most rows have distinct_id_kind == variable;
+ // fail when the dominant pattern is "missing" or "literal"
```

**Rails posthog_distinct_id returns the email** [cm#85](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/85) [cm#101](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/101)
Silent: every exception and event is keyed on PII, an email change splits the person, and email-or-Integer fallbacks fragment people further.
```diff
- # app/models/user.rb
- def posthog_distinct_id
-   identity&.email_address || id   # email, else Integer pk
- end
- // frontend: posthog.identify(user.email)
+ # The primary key, not the email: an email can change, which would split one
+ # person's history in two, and it is PII on every event's identity.
+ def posthog_distinct_id
+   id.to_s
+ end
+ // frontend: posthog.identify(user.id.to_s)
```

**Rails job errors carry no user** [cm#85](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/85)
Silent: failed-job and exception events reach Error Tracking with no person attached.
```diff
- class ExampleJob < ApplicationJob
-   def perform(distinct_id, should_fail: false)
-     raise 'Job failed'   # captured, but with no user attached
-   end
- end
+ class ExampleJob < ApplicationJob
+   posthog_distinct_id ->(distinct_id, *) { distinct_id }
+   def perform(distinct_id, should_fail: false)
+     raise StandardError, 'Example job failure' if should_fail
+   end
+ end
```

**CLI generates a new id every run** 
Every invocation is a new person, so retention and per-user counts are meaningless; OS usernames add PII.
```diff
- posthog.capture(
-     distinct_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),   # new person on every call
-     event="todo_added",
- )
+ def get_user_id():
+     """Uses a UUID stored in the data file to represent this user."""
+     if DATA_FILE.exists():
+         data = json.loads(DATA_FILE.read_text())
+         if 'user_id' in data:
+             return data['user_id']
```

**Stripe metadata gets a different id than identify** [cm#106](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/106) [cm#107](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/107)
Silent: revenue never joins to the person who paid, Top Customers and persons_revenue_analytics stay empty or wrong, and the bad metadata blocks correct identification later.
```diff
- // app calls posthog.identify(user.email, ...)
- const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({
-   client_reference_id: org.id,
-   metadata: { posthog_person_distinct_id: user.stripeCustomerId },
- })
- // or: posthog_person_distinct_id: user.distinct_id || user.email
+ // find it first: posthog.identify(<first arg>, ...) is the distinct_id
+ // never infer it from client_reference_id (it MAY NOT be the distinct_id)
+ const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({
+   client_reference_id: distinctId,   // set so webhooks can read it
+   metadata: { posthog_person_distinct_id: distinctId }, // threaded from a caller
+ })
```

**Placeholder distinct id written to Stripe** [cm#112](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/112) [cm#107](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/107)
Silent: every customer is tagged with the same fake id, nothing joins, and the missing identity is hidden.
```diff
- const customer = await stripe.customers.create({
-   email,
-   metadata: { posthog_person_distinct_id: 'TODO_POSTHOG_DISTINCT_ID' },
- })
+ // distinct_id not in scope: thread it from a caller as an optional parameter.
+ // No caller has it: skip the call site and leave a TODO comment.
+ // No distinct_id anywhere: [ABORT] Could not find a PostHog distinct_id
+ // (Tenet 1 still says a TODO_POSTHOG_DISTINCT_ID string is the fallback)
```

**Revenue setup aborts when users are never identified** [wizard#389](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/pull/389)
Revenue data never joins to real persons; wrong data, no error.
```diff
- stripe.customers.create({
-   email,
-   metadata: { posthog_distinct_id: email },   // invented, no identify() anywhere
- })
+ [ABORT] Could not find a PostHog distinct_id
+ -> "Your users must be identified in PostHog before they can be tagged in Stripe."
+ [ABORT] Could not find a Stripe integration
```

**Elixir context lost in spawned processes** [cm#154](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/154) [cm#268](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/268)
Silent: captures from a Task or job carry no distinct_id or request context, and capture returns an error nobody checks.
```diff
- PostHog.set_context(%{distinct_id: user.id})   # plug process
- Task.start(fn ->
-   PostHog.capture("export_finished")           # other process: no context
- end)
+ Task.start(fn ->
+   PostHog.set_context(%{distinct_id: user.id}) # set in the capturing process
+   PostHog.capture("export_finished")
+ end)
+ # or pass distinct_id explicitly on the capture
```

**Spans not joined to person or replay** [cm#391](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/391) [cm#399](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/399)
Silent: spans appear in Tracing but cannot be tied to a person or a Session Replay recording.
```diff
- with posthog.start_span("checkout"):   # no context: no distinct id, no session id
-     process_order(order)
+ with posthog.new_context():
+     posthog.identify_context(user_id)
+     posthog.set_context_session(session_id)
+     with posthog.start_span("checkout"):
+         process_order(order)
+ # Django: contexts middleware does this per request
```

items.title: feat(web): Navigate Canvas and project Code with real Git authority
items.body:
## Product contract

Use the checkout serving Raven: `F:/segundodvt/dvt`. Canvas, Code and Model share retained navigation/editor state. Code access follows the existing scoped file authority: writable files retain guarded save/CAS; genuinely read-only files remain read-only.

Current user-approved interaction supersedes the early catalogue wording: one Models list, with Source represented as a model property/badge, and shared project Connections. Click selects/opens Properties; it must not create an instance. Placement uses drag or the explicit accessible Add command. Availability, registered definition and placed instance stay distinct; placement retains scoped references, copies no SQL and creates no original-to-instance edge. See integrated #3834/#3815 and the exact contemporary evidence, rather than reapplying the older click-to-create description.

Later Code compile/materialize and file-creation actions are delivered by #3883/#3886; these do not by themselves provide real project Git authority or native graph-to-dbt publication. The historical bounded-cut record below remains attributed to its original SHAs.

Git must mean a real scoped project repository, initially local with branch main and no remote, configurable later. Native publication must produce a governed project artifact while retaining ADR-0064 Substrait authority. Filesystem browsing does not deliver that remaining Git contract.

## Integrated bounded cut

- Serving checkout: `F:/segundodvt/dvt`; local branch `main`, synchronized with `origin/main` and clean.
- [PR #3805](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/pull/3805) merged at **2026-11-06 21:05:18 UTC** as `c1ab9f4bc403b9a8895951f7e7a8bcacf147288c`.
- Validated base `650a6b24aadeaac755d5ffd4054afcfa85647c42` → published source head `0cc1fc5d0c6f9bbf181b0ff9087fe0b3e6820c85`: **350 paths**. Merged and validated source trees are identical: `a290fa7d536a507aaecce5f2f31d7b6b2e3cb0fa`.
- Complete committed-head `pnpm verify:prepush` and enabled push passed: **723 native manifests, 6,492 Web cases, 231 Cypress cases across 88 specs**, with no pending/skipped Cypress case. Disposable database leases were retired. [Published local evidence](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6694901847).
- Fresh actual premerge `GIT_BASE=650a6b24aadeaac755d5ffd4054afcfa85647c42 GIT_HEAD=0cc1fc5d0c6f9bbf181b0ff9087fe0b3e6820c85 pnpm docs:feature-mechanization:implementation` passed **723 manifests** at 20:44:56 UTC with a clean tree, without import/rebuild. Both identities remained unchanged through merge.
- All seven required PR checks passed and the current-authority Code review thread is resolved. [Final acceptance](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/pull/3805#issuecomment-6695561081). Initial CI failures and artifacts remain disclosed: the two unchanged repetitions passed 38/38 available and 56/56 controlled cases, plus 9/9 unchanged movement cases locally; no source fix for their intermittent causes is claimed.
- Native CAS reconciled Code-guide declarations and exact ownership, including removal of the shared adapter's competing file-authority claim; no import/rebuild or source-policy downgrade.
- Post-merge Raven `/canvas`, API `/healthz` and worker `/readyz` return **HTTP 200**. Only `dvt-postgres` and `dvt-planning-db-postgres` remain running, healthy, with their original container identities and persistent data mounts. Removed local test Docker containers were not recreated.

The bounded cut delivers one Elements definition catalogue and independent native instances, read-only Code with inline reference cards, guarded dbt project-root relocation and shared pointer/keyboard/free-camera behavior. Placement preserves scoped definitions, copies no SQL and creates no original-to-instance edge. Scoped Source/dbt Reads feed native Model Output and retain their authoring state across Apply/reopen.

Native compilation reuses the existing bounded analyzer cache with complete source/scope/root/profile/environment/operation/selector identities and single-flight. Dynamic inputs bypass reuse. Browser Code persistence restores only schema-validated ready evidence bound to revision and model identities, never a compiled boolean. Moving cards or declaring an unused Source does not invalidate an unchanged saved output sample. Changed used inputs and output semantics still invalidate it.

## Current evidence and limitations

- Current review correction: [prospective current-authority design](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6692187384). **34** Code/ownership/catalogue cases pass, including three warm-cache revalidation negatives; **two** complete native Chrome cases pass in 21 seconds, including original placement and relocated Code across two full navigations. Web package lint/typecheck and strict touched-surface lint pass. **27** unchanged contract cases, contract lint/types and ADR-0000 traceability pass for the two header corrections.
- Latest bounded cleanup: [prospective destination correction](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6670520400), [schema admission and explicit ownership](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6671058356), [committed results](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6671333951).
- Earlier destination-focused proof: Web unit **74**, authoring presentation **6**, provenance architecture **2**, API publisher/selection **16** pass. Strict touched-source Web/API ESLint and both package typechecks pass. The new publisher negative failed before the fix and passes afterwards.
- Native operation-session completion: [prospective design](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6689544902), [committed six-case result](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6689734247). Seven test lines complete the public Model transaction after the existing assertions; production navigation protection is unchanged.
- Native component `SYS-WEB-CANVAS-CONNECTION-PROVENANCE` owns the one pure resolver, its actual inspector call relation and required graph test. Existing InspectCanvasNode and ConfigureCanvasDvtNode reference rails are revision 6; no parallel product command/query or connection authority.
- Actual shared Raven: governed destination is selected and saved as `local-postgres-proof → public.model_1_result`. Protected Model 1 row sampling returns **5 rows / 6 columns in 122 ms**. **Execution Preview remains rejected**: `amount` is PostgreSQL `numeric`, outside the current bounded publication schema. Rejection occurs before SQL artifact storage; UI explains unsupported/unresolved types. No Run/target write, numeric-to-float coercion or fabricated digest. Numeric publication requires a coherent provider/profile contract extension.
- The earlier bounded source audit reported no Web exact-body duplicate groups. Whole-code scan still finds **9 pre-existing method groups** in older proof-runner lifecycle/bootstrap code; these are unchanged method bodies, disclosed in ED/risk rather than claimed removed. Sixteen copied HTTP parsers, four output-reader copies and both duplicated Canvas test normalizers were removed in the bounded branch cleanup. Native rail duplicate query returns no rows.
- Governance refresh: **5,975 governed / 0 ungoverned / 0 drift**, stable after two passes. ARC-2 remains; existing evidence/risk updated.
- Prior-head package, native browser, compile reuse and movement evidence remains in the issue journal. The interrupted full runs passed large earlier phases but do not certify this head. Exact-base/head native acceptance and the complete gate are recorded in the final PR acceptance linked above.
- Earlier real native clone: seven analysis calls used three processes; repeat reads 48–54 ms. Actual application observations included cold Model sample 14,517 ms, refresh 203 ms and inner Read 122 ms. These are observations, not latency guarantees; rows are not cached.
- The approved local dev target is `local-postgres-proof`. Native dbt parent views and prior protected data-file repair remain separate recorded actions; Preview does not materialize dependencies implicitly.

## Acceptance still open

- Coherent numeric/decimal publication support; current sampling works, configured publication remains rejected for those types.
- Real scoped project Git initialization and branch/HEAD/index/status/history.
- Native graph-to-dbt model publication while retaining ADR-0064 semantic authority.

**Keep #3747 open after this bounded merge** for Git/publication acceptance. A file explorer does not deliver Git. Nine prior related PRs are merged and their two review threads are resolved on the base.

## Governing sources and limits

AGENTS.md; governance inventory; AI work protocol; PR preflight/CI triage; ADR-0060/0061/0064; command/query and Fowler governance; existing Planning DB authority and component guides. ARC-2: `docs/evidence/ED-20261102-dbt-project-root-relocation.md` and `docs/risk-register/dbt-project-root-relocation-20261102.md`.

GitHub owns delivery, Planning DB architecture/rails and Git physical source. No DB import/rebuild, duplicated query/cache, stub/placeholder, new debt, relaxed rule/deadline/size bound or bypassed hook. Existing React-act/chart-dimension/Vite warnings remain disclosed. Failed, interrupted, partial and older-head results remain failed/partial evidence.
