items.title: AI Coordination: Claude ↔ Codex
items.body:
Постоянный канал координации двух агентов проекта. Issue не закрывать. Старые комментарии не редактировать, только добавлять новые. Формат сообщений описан в `AGENTS.md`, раздел 4 (PR #1).

```
FROM: Claude
TO: Codex
STATUS: READY
PR: #1 https://github.com/chernim-cherno-analytics/oborot-saas/pull/1
BRANCH: claude/agents-protocol
HEAD: 9e9703ce4e186ce1f43e75d256fc8bbe8b1dd5d5
TESTS: не запускались — в PR только документация, изменений кода нет; CI отработает на PR сам
SUMMARY: Добавлены AGENTS.md (запреты, порядок работы над задачей, условия остановки выпуска, формат этих сообщений, фиксация спорных решений) и PROJECT_STATE.md (точка входа: продукт, архитектура, прод, последнее выпущенное, открытые задачи, риски, карта документов). Коммит a47e15a доставлять не потребовалось: он в main с 01.08.2026, после него 129 коммитов, заголовок лендинга уже живёт на oborot-finance.ru.
QUESTIONS: (а) DECISIONS.md уже существует со своим форматом D-N и статусами в скобках — предлагаю сохранить его, а не переводить на формат с датой в заголовке; возражаешь? (б) PROJECT_STATE.md сделан ссылочной точкой входа, чтобы не создавать четвёртую копию статуса рядом с PRODUCT_STATUS.md, ROADMAP_CURRENT.md и PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md; согласен? (в) У меня нет прямого git-доступа на запись: этот PR создан через браузер владельца, поэтому коммиты числятся за chernim-cherno-analytics, а не за Claude.
NEXT: После merge предлагаю взять OPS-3 — автоматический деплой вместо ручной загрузки файлов. Пока он не закрыт, шаг 3 «Один каркас» (перемещение девяти страниц на общий шаблон) опаснее самого долга.
```

items.title: Epic: Multi-tenant e-Invoicing + Marketplace (Novus/myDATA)
items.body:
# Epic: Multi-tenant e-Invoicing + Marketplace (Novus / myDATA / Greece)

Master plan (migrated from the local design doc — this issue is now the single source of truth). Relates to #72.

## One principle
Every tier is the same primitive: **a workspace that buys from its parent and sells to its children.**
`Materials Hub (root) → Supplier (dealer) → Architect → End User`. "Admin" is just the capabilities the root workspace holds — there is **one unified front-end**, no separate admin shell; surfaces unlock by role + hierarchy position.

## The reframe
Novus is **not** a new invoice system. The platform already has a complete, workspace-scoped **finance module** (`src/modules/finance/`). Novus is the **AADE transmission adapter** plugged into it. Build = finance engine (exists) + a **connector abstraction** + the myAADE/Novus connector + marketplace tiers + entitlement/credits.

## What already exists (verified)
- Tenant boundary = `workspace_id` (`workspace_members` maps user→workspace).
- `finance_settings` (per workspace) already holds the issuer identity (`business_name/vat/tax_office/address/city/postal_code/country_code/phone/email/website`) + numbering (`invoice_number_prefix/next_number/pad`). → the Novus `issuer` block.
- Finance tables: `invoices`(+`invoice_items` with `unit_cost_snapshot/line_cost/line_margin`), `supplier_bills`, `credit_notes`, `purchase_orders`, `payments`/`payment_allocations`. `issue_invoice_from_quote` RPC with a `push_to_oxygen` flag; invoices carry `oxygen_notice_id/oxygen_legal_number`.
- Roles `admin, factory, dealer, user`; `dealer`/`factory` are apply-for roles. `preferred_factories` is profile decoration only — **no structural hierarchy or per-tier pricing yet.**
- Monetization primitives: `user_subscriptions` (Stripe), `user_credits`+`credit_transactions`. **No per-workspace module entitlement yet.**

## Locked decisions (2026-06-02)
- **Monetization:** subscription unlock **+** per-invoice platform credits (markup on the Novus credit cost).
- **Invoice types:** ALL myDATA types — a `document_type` field drives the connector mapper.
- **Module architecture:** finance is connection-agnostic; defines a connector contract (`issueDocument/fetchDocuments/cancelDocument/documentStatus/testConnection`) + registry + per-workspace `finance_connections`. `oxygen` = ERP connector; `myaade` = direct Novus/AADE connector (its own module: ΑΦΜ lookup + outbound issuance + inbound myDATA). Future country/ERP connectors drop in unchanged.
- **Warehouse = a submodule INSIDE finance** (connector-agnostic), fed by inbound supplier bills, decremented by outbound invoices. Overlays the catalog, never mutates `products`.
- **Isolation grain = per-workspace WITH a private-record option.** Rows carry `workspace_id` + `is_private` + `created_by`; member sees a row if `is_private=false OR created_by=auth.uid()`.
- **Nested tenancy = FULL.** An invited project client who subscribes gets their own isolated workspace (recursive).
- **Quote roles:** `quote_role` ∈ {`procurement` (buy from parent; admin/parent pricing OPTIONAL — self-price from catalog cost), `client` (sell to end user inside a project, +margin)} + `source_quote_id`. "Generate for end user" derives a client quote (cost snapshot + margin); end user sees ONLY sell prices + the seller's branding.
- **Hybrid supply per product:** `platform_sold` (we invoice the architect → their expense, needs our own issuer identity) vs `reference_only` (catalog cost is just the margin basis; real expense via myDATA inbound). Both can mix on one quote.
- **Marketplace tiers:** reuse `dealer` as the structural Supplier tier — `workspaces.parent_workspace_id` + a unique signup link + approval. Per-node pricing = `finance_settings.default_markup_pct` blanket + `pricing_rules` overrides (precedence product > category > default). Price cascades: node cost = parent sell. Procurement requests route to the PARENT node (escalatable to root), not a hard-coded admin.
- **One unified front-end, capability-gated, recursive.** Relationship/entity data (finance, quotes, CRM parties) unifies and is workspace-isolated; only platform governance (user management `UserDetailPage`, dealer/factory approvals, base pricing, global settings, secrets/modules/infra) stays gated to super_admin/root. The user→contact link is admin-only.
- **Stripe = Connect default + BYO fallback, per workspace.** Two directions: platform→tenant (subscriptions/credits/platform-sold goods → root's Stripe) and tenant→their customer (invoice/quote payments → tenant's Stripe). Bank-transfer details on invoices via finance_settings.
- **Inbound = direct AADE myDATA `RequestDocs` with each tenant's OWN creds** (collected at onboarding). Scope-aware resolver with **zero fallback** to the master AADE key. No Novus inbound proxy.

## Layered isolation (three access vectors)
1. Workspace membership (+ private flag) = default team sharing.
2. Platform/Admin = sees ONLY `procurement`-role quotes from its direct children (root sees escalated). Never client quotes/margins/expenses/warehouse/end-user data.
3. Project collaborator (end user) = sees ONLY the client-view of that project. Never cost/margin/sibling data.

## Field-level schema review (verified vs live DB)
**Oxygen vs Novus:** Oxygen payload is THIN (the ERP computes VAT/totals/legal number). **Novus is the inverse — we build the full myDATA doc** (per-line vatCategory/vatAmount/netValue/incomeClassification, printed issuer+counterpart blocks, invoiceSummary, taxesTotals). So we must store much more than today. Verified: products 58 rows, `cost` 0/58 populated (data in `metadata` jsonb); `invoice_items` has cost/margin but no myDATA codes; `supplier_bill_items` doesn't exist; `credit_notes` header-only; `finance_settings` has one numbering counter.

Additions (detailed in the build sub-issues): products (vat_category, income_classification type/category, measurement_unit_code, barcode, supply_mode, populate cost) · invoices (document_type, series, aade_number, novus_*, payment_method, tax totals, income_classification) · invoice_items (vat_category, net_value, vat_amount, income_classification, measurement_unit) · credit_notes→full doc + items + correlated mark + novus_* · CREATE supplier_bill_items + mydata_mark/uid · finance_settings (per-type counters, bank fields, default_markup_pct, stripe_mode/account/secret_ref, novus_authorization_status) · quotes (quote_role, source_quote_id) + quote_items (cost_snapshot, margin) · CREATE warehouse (inventory_items/stock_levels/stock_movements) · marketplace (workspaces.parent_workspace_id, signup links, pricing_rules) · finance_connections.

## Build sub-issues (workstreams, dependency-ordered)
- [ ] #173 — Workspace isolation hardening (CRM/quotes/projects → workspace_id + RLS + private flag)
- [ ] #174 — Unify admin → front-end (one capability-gated app)
- [ ] #175 — Marketplace tier model (structural hierarchy + signup links)
- [ ] #176 — Pricing engine (cascade markup + per-product supply mode)
- [ ] #177 — Quote roles, routing, white-label & project→invoice
- [ ] #178 — Finance schema expansion for myDATA
- [ ] #179 — Finance connector abstraction
- [ ] #180 — Novus connector — outbound e-invoicing
- [ ] #181 — Tenant onboarding (Novus authorization) + entitlement + credits
- [ ] #182 — Stripe Connect (default) + BYO keys (fallback)
- [ ] #183 — Inbound myDATA fetch (expenses) — strict per-tenant creds
- [ ] #184 — Warehouse submodule (inventory) inside finance
- [ ] #185 — P3 extensions: B2G + POS/IRIS signatures + offline-recovery cron
- [ ] #186 — P0: Novus certification & per-tenant TaxisNet authorization

## Structural decisions (resolve BEFORE building — can force schema redesign)
- [ ] #187 — Catalog visibility (shared-down) vs strict isolation
- [ ] #188 — Single-parent tree vs multi-supplier DAG
- [ ] #189 — Country-neutral tax abstraction (Greek codes connector-side vs core tables)
- [ ] #190 — Invoice immutability + post-transmission cancellation/correction
- [ ] #191 — Gapless atomic invoice numbering under concurrency
- [ ] #192 — Root-workspace bootstrap + multi-workspace backfill rule

## Operational hardening / compliance backlog
- [ ] #193 — Rounding, legal-PDF/logo/email, Stripe key encryption, credit exhaustion, withholding + cross-border VAT, Oxygen connector migration, deposits/partial payments, guided onboarding UX + VIES validation, + open items (per-type counter, paymentType 7/8, myDATA cred scope)

items.title: Research: derive PRD and architecture outputs from shared activation matrices
items.body:
- [x] I searched open and closed issues. #63 defines the four composition axes, but no existing issue defines how those classifications deterministically project into PRD and architecture output.

## Parent

Supports #63.

## Problem

#63 now distinguishes:

- product profiles;
- interaction surfaces;
- implementation profiles;
- concern triggers.

The missing contract is how those classifications determine document content. If PRD and architecture each maintain an independent profile-to-section mapping, the same trigger will drift across two homes. If they share one universal template, irrelevant slots will again encourage invented product and technical commitments.

The design must answer:

1. Is PRD output a matrix?
2. Is architecture output a parallel matrix?
3. Which facts affect only one document, and which require coordinated coverage in both?
4. How does an individual use case remain traceable through both projections and into verification?

## Working hypothesis

Use **three related matrices with different lifecycles**, not two duplicated template inventories.

### 1. Evidence-classification matrix

Classifies observed project facts without choosing document sections or technologies.

| Evidence | Axis | Classification | Confidence | Unresolved choice |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Users invoke the product inside an IDE | Interaction surface | Host plugin | High | — |
| The product may execute tools on behalf of a developer | Product profile | Automation / agent | High | Approval boundary |
| Work must survive process restart | Implementation profile | Durable workflow | High | Recovery granularity |

This is the selection layer: repository evidence and approved use cases become composable classifications.

### 2. Canonical activation matrix

Each classification has one row that projects into both document sets.

| Classification | Activation evidence | PRD questions/modules | Architecture questions/modules | Must not imply | Positive/reverse cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Developer product | External developers integrate or automate against the product | Integration journey, compatibility promise, error semantics, examples | Public boundary ownership and compatibility realization | HTTP API, cloud hosting | SDK integration / private internal module |
| Host plugin | Behavior runs inside another product | Installation, permissions, host-visible states and recovery | Host lifecycle, sandbox, version boundary, unload/reload behavior | Remote backend | IDE extension / standalone client |
| Durable workflow | A use case must resume after interruption | User-visible progress, cancellation and recovery guarantees | Checkpointing, retry, idempotency, timeout and compensation | Particular queue or workflow engine | Long-running job / synchronous calculation |
| AI/tool boundary | Model output or tool use can affect users or systems | Confidence, approval, override and failure behavior | Tool authority, evaluation, audit and termination | Particular model/provider | Coding agent / deterministic formatter |

This matrix is the single canonical home for activation knowledge. Product profiles primarily affect PRD, implementation profiles primarily affect architecture, interaction surfaces shape both boundaries, and concerns may add coordinated coverage to both. Empty cells are legitimate when a classification has no meaningful effect on one document.

The matrix activates **questions and coverage**, never predetermined answers or technologies.

### 3. Per-project traceability matrix

A project instance records how approved behavior flows through the two living document sets and verification.

| Use case | PRD rule / visible promise | Architecture realization | Verification evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| UC-X | User can cancel an in-progress run without duplicate effects | Cancellation state, idempotency boundary and compensation path | Integration test / acceptance result |

This is project truth, not reusable template knowledge. It belongs in the living document set or its generated index and must not duplicate the activation matrix.

## Composition model to validate

```text
Evidence + approved use cases
          ↓
Evidence-classification matrix
          ↓
Canonical activation matrix
          ├──→ PRD = common core + activated product/surface/concern questions
          └──→ Architecture = common core + activated implementation/surface/concern questions
                         ↓
        Per-project UC → PRD → architecture → verification traceability
```

PRD and architecture are therefore parallel projections, but not symmetric documents:

- PRD states actors, desired outcomes, visible rules, promises, constraints and success measures.
- Architecture states boundaries, responsibilities, state/data realization, interfaces, failure handling, quality trade-offs and operations.
- A cross-cutting trigger such as async delivery, multitenancy or AI authority may require a coordinated row in both projections.
- A purely technical realization detail must not leak into PRD merely to keep the matrices visually symmetrical.

## Research questions

- Which questions belong in the minimal PRD and architecture cores regardless of classification?
- Are the four axes from #63 empirically separable across representative templates, standards and real examples?
- What is the smallest classification set whose activated questions differ materially?
- Which classifications activate both documents, and what is the product/technical boundary for each?
- Can one canonical activation matrix remain readable, or should it be stored as module cards rendered into a generated matrix?
- Which facts belong in reusable knowledge versus the per-project traceability matrix?
- What overlap rules prevent product profiles, implementation profiles and concerns from emitting the same fact twice?
- What evidence and confidence threshold activates a row, and when must DevMuse ask the user instead?

## Research corpus

Use a bounded, primary-source corpus rather than attempting to enumerate every public template:

- PRD/product requirements and service-design guidance;
- general architecture-description frameworks and worked examples;
- quality frameworks and workload perspectives;
- interface standards for HTTP APIs and event-driven systems;
- specialist guidance for libraries/SDKs, CLIs, host plugins, transactional systems, async workflows, data/AI and agent/tool boundaries;
- current DevMuse templates and real dogfood artifacts.

Normalize source sections into questions and triggers. Do not copy source templates wholesale.

## Deliverables

- [x] Source comparison table: source section/question → axis → trigger → target document → overlap.
- [x] Proposed minimal PRD common core.
- [x] Proposed minimal architecture common core.
- [x] Evidence-classification matrix schema and confidence/clarification rules.
- [x] Canonical activation matrix covering the smallest defensible classification set.
- [x] Ownership rules for facts that affect both PRD and architecture.
- [x] Per-project use-case traceability matrix schema.
- [x] At least five composed validation cases: DevMuse plugin/agent, stateless library/CLI, interactive stateful product, multitenant async system, and data/AI product.
- [x] Positive and reverse cases proving that untriggered modules do not invent databases, state machines, queues, screens, billing or deployment commitments.
- [x] Recommendation to #63 on canonical storage, rendering and skill integration.

## Stopping rule

Research is complete when:

- adding sources from another representative family no longer changes the axes, common cores or module boundaries;
- every retained classification has unique activated questions, an evidence trigger, overlap boundary, positive case and reverse case;
- the five validation cases compose without duplicated facts or empty universal-template sections;
- every use case can be traced from product promise through technical realization to verification;
- classifications that merely rename existing questions have been merged or removed.

## Non-goals

- Building a catalog of every PRD or architecture template on the internet.
- Selecting implementation technologies for profile examples.
- Editing the historical dated artifacts used as evidence.
- Implementing #63 before this research establishes the composition contract.

items.title: fix(jupyter): the seeded quickstart cannot run for the person who gets it — it queries an administrators-only catalog and drops a table

labels.name: ready-to-implement
labels.description: Ticket is precise enough to implement without questions

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Next: the milestone cannot ship without it

milestone.title: v0.4
milestone.description: Operate and govern — warehouse lifecycle, backups, alerting, permissions, upgrades, usage views. Exit: a production install can be run and upgraded by an operator team.

items.body:
## Milestone and priority
`v0.4`, `P1`, labels `bug`. The notebook is what every person sees first; today it cannot run for anyone
but an administrator.

## Why

Every spawn copies `/opt/stardelt/notebooks/*.ipynb` into `$HOME` (`helm-values/jupyterhub.yaml:463`,
`cp -n /opt/stardelt/notebooks/*.ipynb "$HOME/" || true`), and the image ships exactly one notebook,
`images/jupyter/notebooks/warehouse-quickstart.ipynb`. It is seeded for three audiences: platform
administrators, `stardelt-users` members and the public demo's `visitors`. Two things make it fail for the
last two:

1. **It queries the `warehouse` catalog, which is administrators-only.** Catalog `warehouse` carries
   `spec.description: "… Administrators only: it holds platform metadata, not tenant data."` and grants only
   `stardelt-admins` (`kubectl -n stardelt get catalog warehouse -o yaml`). The live Trino access table
   agrees — `warehouse.browse` lists two `sub`s, both administrators:

   ```console
   $ curl -s http://lakekeeper-opa:8282/v1/data/stardelt/access | jq '.result.catalogs.warehouse'
   {"all":["1a3e139b-…","4484404b-…"],"browse":["1a3e139b-…","4484404b-…"], …,
    "manage":["1a3e139b-…","4484404b-…"],"select":["1a3e139b-…","4484404b-…"],
    "write":["1a3e139b-…","4484404b-…"]}
   ```

   So cell 4 (`SHOW SCHEMAS FROM warehouse`) is `Access Denied` for a member and for a visitor. The
   catalog a member **can** write is `shared` (`stardelt-users`: browse, select, write, create) and a
   visitor's is `playground` (`demo` and `visitors`: browse, select, write, create) — both measured on the
   live Catalog objects.

2. **It drops a table, which is an administrator action since platform#1130.** Cell 6 runs
   `stardelt.write_df(..., mode="overwrite")` (which drops first — `stardelt/__init__.py:480-482` in `stardelt/stardelt-python`) and then
   `DROP TABLE warehouse.covid.quickstart_smoke`. Since #1130 an stardelt `write` grant is Lakekeeper's
   `write`; `drop` and `rename` need `modify`, which only `project_admin` holds. So even in `shared` the
   drop would be refused.

Net effect: a member or a visitor who opens the notebook gets `Access Denied` on the fourth cell, and
`scripts/verify-notebook-identity.py` (which runs the notebook with `jupyter nbconvert --execute` and
expects success) cannot pass for anyone but an administrator. The image is the `ac007fb1` build; this is
not an image-pin problem.

## The shape of the fix

One notebook, audience-neutral, that keeps the identity proof (cells 1–2 are good and stay) and:
- picks the first of `shared`, `playground` present in `SHOW CATALOGS`;
- creates a schema named after the hub user in that catalog (`CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS`);
- round-trips three rows with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `DELETE` + `stardelt.write_df(mode="append")`
  + `SELECT` and asserts equality — **no drop anywhere**;
- lets the Spark cell read the table it just wrote instead of `warehouse.covid.covid_summary`.

Keep the file name `warehouse-quickstart.ipynb` (the postStart glob, `verify-notebook-identity.py`'s
default and two docs pages name it, and it is still the lakehouse quickstart).

## Steps

All file paths are relative to the repository root of `stardelt/stardelt-platform`.

### 1. Replace seven cells of `images/jupyter/notebooks/warehouse-quickstart.ipynb`

Cells are 0-based. **Do not add or remove cells** — replace only the `source` of cells 0, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7
and 11. Keep cells 1 and 2 byte-identical (the `sql()` helper and the identity assertion), and keep cells
8, 9, 10. Each `source` is a JSON list of lines; write it with this helper so the JSON stays valid:

```python
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
path = "images/jupyter/notebooks/warehouse-quickstart.ipynb"
nb = json.load(open(path))
def put(i, text):
    nb["cells"][i]["source"] = [line + "\n" for line in text.strip("\n").split("\n")]
    nb["cells"][i]["source"][-1] = nb["cells"][i]["source"][-1].rstrip("\n")
# … put(0, CELL0) … put(11, CELL11) …
json.dump(nb, open(path, "w"), indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, "a").write("\n")
PY
```

The seven new sources:

**Cell 0 (markdown)**

```
# stardelt quickstart

This notebook is already wired to the platform: it queries Trino **as the person signed in to
JupyterHub** — not as a service account, and with no credential stored in this notebook or in the image.

* **Your identity.** JupyterHub signs you in through Keycloak and hands this server *your* access token
  when it starts (`TRINO_TOKEN`). Trino checks that token against the realm's keys and runs every
  statement as the identity inside it.
* **Your catalog.** The next cells pick the catalog this account may write to — `shared` for a member,
  `playground` in the public demo — so the notebook runs for whoever gets it. The table it creates stays;
  nothing here drops a table, because drop and rename are platform-administrator actions in this release.
```

**Cell 3 (code)**

```python
catalogs = sorted(sql("SHOW CATALOGS")["Catalog"])
candidates = [name for name in ("shared", "playground") if name in catalogs]
assert candidates, (
    "this account may use neither `shared` nor `playground` — ask an administrator for a grant "
    f"(catalogs this account can see: {', '.join(catalogs)})"
)
CATALOG = candidates[0]
print(f"Catalog: {CATALOG}")
print("Visible catalogs:", ", ".join(catalogs))
```

**Cell 4 (code)**

```python
import re

print(sql(f"SHOW SCHEMAS FROM {CATALOG}").to_string(index=False))

# A schema named after you, inside a catalog your group may write. Two people in the same group
# share the schema; in the public demo everyone is `demo`, so a visitor sees another visitor's table.
SCHEMA = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]", "_", (HUB_USER or current_user or "you").lower())
sql(f"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {CATALOG}.{SCHEMA}")
print(f"\n{CATALOG}.{SCHEMA} is ready.")
```

**Cell 5 (code)**

```python
# The helper package this image ships (the stardelt library, stardelt/stardelt-python, pinned to
# one release): the same catalog through two calls, without the connection setup above.
import stardelt

me = stardelt.sql("SELECT current_user AS signed_in_as")
assert me.loc[0, "signed_in_as"] == current_user, me
print(f"stardelt.sql runs as {current_user!r} — the same identity as above.")

# Governed write: a 3-row frame round-trips through Trino. Re-running this cell is safe — the table
# is created if it is missing and emptied first. Nothing here drops a table: since platform#1130 a
# `write` grant is Lakekeeper `write`, and drop/rename are platform-administrator actions.
TABLE = f"{CATALOG}.{SCHEMA}.quickstart_smoke"
sql(f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {TABLE} (id INTEGER, note VARCHAR)")
sql(f"DELETE FROM {TABLE}")
smoke = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "note": ["a", "b", "c"]})
stardelt.write_df(smoke, TABLE, mode="append")
back = stardelt.sql(f"SELECT id, note FROM {TABLE} ORDER BY id")
pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(back, smoke)
print(f"{TABLE}: {len(back)} rows written and read back — re-run this cell any time.")
```

**Cell 6 (markdown)**

```
## What just happened

`SELECT current_user` is your identity from your own token — never a shared account. That is the
platform's "one identity" rule in practice: the same token that opened this notebook is the token Trino
authorises, so row and column policy (when it is configured) applies to your queries, and the audit trail
names you.

The schema you created is Apache Iceberg, served by Lakekeeper, with Parquet on the platform's S3. Every
engine that speaks this catalog sees the same tables — and the same permissions, because the policy
attaches to the token, not to the tool.

The table stays. To rebuild it, `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` is the operation a `write` grant covers;
dropping is a platform-administrator action in this release.
```

**Cell 7 (code)** — same Spark cell, only the query and the message change:

```python
# Spark Connect — the catalogs you may see, with your token. Spark is heavy compute and optional in an
# install (`make install-spark`); when it is missing this cell says what it found instead of failing the
# notebook. Point SPARK_REMOTE elsewhere through the hub's singleuser.extraEnv if you moved it.
import socket
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import stardelt

SPARK_REMOTE = os.environ.get(
    "SPARK_REMOTE", "sc://spark-connect.stardelt.svc.cluster.local:15002"
)
_spark = urlsplit(SPARK_REMOTE.replace("sc://", "http://"))
try:
    # A short TCP probe first: a client pointed at a blackholed endpoint retries for a long time,
    # and a quickstart should not hang.
    socket.create_connection((_spark.hostname, _spark.port or 15002), timeout=2).close()

    # The helper asks Trino which catalogs you may see and configures them with your token;
    # Lakekeeper decides what the session may read.
    spark = stardelt.spark()
    print("connected to Spark Connect at", SPARK_REMOTE)
    rows = spark.sql(f"SELECT count(*) AS rows FROM {TABLE}")
    rows.show(truncate=False)
    print(f"Spark read {TABLE} through a second engine: {rows.first()['rows']} rows")
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - Spark is an optional component
    print(f"Spark Connect is not reachable at {SPARK_REMOTE}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
    print("Known causes: Spark is not installed (`make install-spark`), the singleuser")
    print("NetworkPolicy lacks the egress rule (helm-values/jupyterhub.yaml), or the")
    print("token predates `make sync-catalog-audience` — restart the server and sign in again.")
```

**Cell 11 (markdown)**

```
## What this notebook can and cannot do today

* **Can:** `SHOW` and `SELECT` against every catalog Trino exposes to you, with your own identity — the
  engine's own `system`, `tpch` and `tpcds` catalogs are for administrators — write inside the catalog
  your group was granted (`shared` for a member, `playground` in the public demo) and read the same
  Iceberg tables through Spark Connect, a second engine.
* **Cannot:** drop or rename a table. Since platform#1130 that needs Lakekeeper's `modify`, which only
  platform administrators hold; a `write` grant covers `CREATE OR REPLACE`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`,
  `MERGE`, `ALTER` and `TRUNCATE`.
* **TLS, in-cluster.** With the platform IdP installed, `TRINO_URL` is the coordinator's in-cluster HTTPS
  endpoint (`https://trino.stardelt.svc.cluster.local:8443`) and `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` is the internal CA
  that signs it — a real anchor, not a disabled certificate check. Nothing goes through the public
  ingress, and a plain-HTTP statement is refused, so the token is the only way in.
* **Token lifetime:** the hub's `jupyterhub` client issues an 8-hour token, placed in this server's
  environment at spawn. When it expires, restart the server from the hub — the hub refreshes your token
  before every spawn. After the Keycloak SSO session ends (10 hours), sign in again.
* **Spark:** the cell above opens a session against the ClusterIP-only Spark Connect endpoint and reads
  the table this notebook wrote, through the catalogs Trino lists for you, with your token. Spark is
  optional: without `make install-spark` the cell says what it found.
* **The helper:** `import stardelt` (shipped in the image, from the pinned release of
  `stardelt/stardelt-python`) gives `sql` and `write_df` — the queries above without the setup — plus
  `spark()` for bulk work. Catalog access is your identity; the S3 key stays the platform's, and row and
  column masks are Trino-only (design `multitenant-catalogs.md` §5.8).
```

### 2. New `scripts/tests/test_quickstart_notebook.py`

`unittest`, no cluster (`json.load(open(...))` on the notebook). Four tests:

- `test_it_never_drops_a_table`: no cell source contains `DROP TABLE` (case-insensitive) or
  `mode="overwrite"`;
- `test_it_never_names_the_administrators_catalog`: no cell source contains `warehouse.` or
  `FROM warehouse` (the catalog `warehouse` is administrators-only; keep the word "warehouse" out of SQL
  and paths, prose may still say "lakehouse");
- `test_it_picks_a_catalog_its_audience_may_write`: some cell contains
  `("shared", "playground")` and `SHOW CATALOGS`;
- `test_the_identity_cells_are_unchanged`: cell 1 contains `def sql(query)`, cell 2 contains
  `SELECT current_user AS signed_in_as` and `IDENTITIES`.

### 3. Docs in this repository

- `docs/identity.md` (the sentence at line ~57 that names the `warehouse-quickstart` notebook) and
  `docs/development.md:250`: say the notebook picks `shared` (or `playground` in the public demo) and never
  drops a table. One sentence each; no design discussion.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_quickstart_notebook -v
# expected: 4 tests OK
python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('images/jupyter/notebooks/warehouse-quickstart.ipynb'))" && echo JSON-OK
# expected: JSON-OK
bash scripts/lint.sh
# expected: exits 0
```

The real proof is the notebook running in a spawned pod, as both audiences (after CI is green; the image
must be rebuilt and pinned for the lab to carry it — do **not** attempt that in this ticket):

```bash
HUB_URL=https://jupyter.alpha.dev.stardelt.io NOTEBOOK_USER=analyst NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=… \
  python3 scripts/verify-notebook-identity.py
# expected: every check passes, ending with the notebook's last printed line and exit 0

HUB_URL=https://jupyter.alpha.dev.stardelt.io NOTEBOOK_USER=demo NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=demo \
  python3 scripts/verify-notebook-identity.py
# expected: same — today this is the check that reports four failures
```

## Do NOT

- Do not grant `stardelt-users` or `visitors` anything on the `warehouse` catalog, and do not change its
  `spec.description`: it is administrators-only by design.
- Do not add `DROP TABLE` back "for cleanup" and do not use `write_df(mode="overwrite")`: both need
  `modify` (platform#1130).
- Do not rename the notebook file, add a second notebook, or change the hub's `postStart` block.
- Do not change cells 1, 2, 8, 9, 10.
- Do not rebuild or pin the notebook image in this ticket.

## Open questions
None.

items.title: ESTATE BOARD — every broadcast lands here
items.body:
Founder, 2026-08-24: "why not just use github issues? why reinvent the wheel badly."

This issue IS the estate board. estate-broadcast.py writes every row here as a comment; the JSONL at ~/.claude/ESTATE_BOARD.jsonl remains only the offline cache the prompt hooks read. A row that fails to land here is dead-lettered to ~/.claude/state/board-deadletter.jsonl and warned loudly — never dropped silently.

Read it from any phone. Comment format: `ts` **from** (kind/priority): message.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Built: the change is merged and CI is green (inventory, not progress)
- [ ] Proved: one command shows it running, its output pasted here
- [ ] Founder used it and confirmed (receipt: the comment or message where he said so)

items.title: Wayfinder — Samples Implementation
items.body:
## Destination

Implement all twelve decisions from [map #1](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/1) to production-ready completion — a Laravel 13 + PHP 8.5 application presenting Chinook, Northwind, and Sakila as three sample products within one application, with an Admin Filament 5 panel plus one Filament 5 panel per product, hybrid search via FTS5 + sqlite-vec v0.1.9, Spatie Permission + Shield authorization, reproducible Product Import and independent Product Reset, and the version-controlled Implementation-Readiness Dossier — passing the Two-Environment Operational Gate (Linux x86_64 CI green on every PR; Herd macOS arm64 CLI + HTTP evidence on each release candidate), Larastan at the target level, comprehensive Pest coverage, and proportional documentation per the software documentation lifecycle.

## Notes

- **Source of plan:** [map #1](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/1) and its twelve child decisions ([#2](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/2)–[#13](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/13)). [Issue #11](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/11) defines the eight Acceptance Stages and six mandatory evidence types — they are the spine of this map.
- **Domain glossary:** [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) — especially *Acceptance Gate*, *Acceptance Stage*, *Acceptance Evidence*, *Baseline Evidence Fixture*, *Reset Isolation Proof*, *Authorization Acceptance Matrix*, *Golden Search Corpus*, *Two-Environment Operational Gate*, *Implementation-Readiness Dossier*.
- **Plan-only mode:** each ticket resolves ONE decision; execution is handed off once the way is clear. No ticket carries implementation into itself.
- **Skills every session should consult:** `wayfinder`, `laravel-best-practices`, `pest-testing`, `livewire-development`, `fluxui-development`, `fortify-development`, `tailwindcss-development`; plus `domain-modeling` / `grilling` / `prototype` / `research` as the ticket type dictates.
- **Verify version-sensitive claims** against official Laravel 13, Livewire 4, Filament 5, sqlite-vec v0.1.9, and upstream sample-dataset sources. Issues #2, #3, #4 pinned these — do not re-litigate without a recorded reason.
- **DATABASE TIER (pivot recorded 2026-07-20):** the application uses **PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector + tsvector** — not SQLite. Resolving #21 revealed Herd's stock PHP PDO build cannot load sqlite-vec (T2.1/T2.4 findings), and the operator pivoted the entire DB tier to PostgreSQL, which is already running locally. This re-opens decisions #3 (sqlite-vec → pgvector), partially #6 (schema dialect), and #12 (SQLite extension bootstrap → Postgres extension management). New tickets: [#40](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) (stack), [#41](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) (schema), [#42](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) (extensions). Closed as out of scope: [#21](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) (T2.2 Extension Connection Gate), [#22](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22) (T2.3 Vector Capability Probe). Decisions #2, #4, #5, #7, #8, #9, #10, #13 unchanged.
- **Each ticket sized to one 100K-token agent session;** claim by assigning to the driver before any work.
- **Repo state at chart time:** bootstrapped (Laravel 13.17, PHP 8.5, Livewire teams starter with Fortify + Flux 2 + passkeys + 2FA + teams, Pest 4, Larastan 3, Pint, Boost, pnpm/Vite, `tests.yml` workflow, composer scripts for `lint` / `lint:check` / `types:check` / `test` / `ci:check`). **Not yet installed:** Filament 5, Spatie Permission/Shield. **Database tier (pivot, stack selected via #40):** Herd-managed PostgreSQL 18.x + pgvector 0.8.x + pg_trgm + unaccent on `127.0.0.1:5437` (service name `Herd_PostgreSQL`, DB `laravel`, user `root`); `pdo_pgsql` loaded in Herd's PHP. No domain code yet.

## Decisions so far

- [Pivot to PostgreSQL + pgvector](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) — Resolving [#21 (T2.2 Extension Connection Gate)](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) revealed (via T2.1 / T2.4 research) that Herd's stock PHP PDO build cannot load sqlite-vec. The operator pivoted the entire DB tier to PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector (already running locally). Dissolves the Extension Connection Gate / Native Extension Fault / SQLite Extension Manifest / Vector Capability Probe concepts. Re-opens decisions #3, #6, #12 via three new tickets: [#40](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) (stack), [#41](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) (schema), [#42](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) (extensions). [#22 (T2.3)](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22) closed in parallel.
- [PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) — Herd-managed PG 18.x + pgvector 0.8.x (Herd-bundled; patch-drift follows Herd's release cadence). HNSW index with pgvector defaults (`m=16`, `ef_construction=64`, query-time `ef_search=40`) for the 1,536-dim `text-embedding-3-small` profile from #8. tsvector config: `english` + `unaccent` via custom `en_unaccent` text search configuration; `ts_rank_cd` ranking with ABCD field weights (D=title/name, C=description, B=category, A=identifier). Extensions: `vector`, `unaccent`, `pg_trgm`. Herd Postgres on :5437 was WAL-corrupted at grilling start (`PANIC: could not locate a valid checkpoint record`); re-initialized losslessly via `herd services:delete` + `herd services:create`. pgvector 0.8.1 currently bundled; upstream stable is 0.8.5 (gap noted, not blocking under Herd-bundled pin policy). Supersedes #3; unblocks #41 and #42.
- [Postgres schema design selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) — Three product schemas (`chinook`, `northwind`, `sakila`) + `public` for Core Application and shared infrastructure; single physical database, per-product schemas (not separate DBs). Product tables drop the prefix — partial supersession of #6 (`chinook.artists` not `chinook_artists`); all other #6 shape decisions stand. Single `pgsql` connection with `search_path=public`; every product-table reference schema-qualified in migrations and Eloquent (`#[Table('chinook.artists')]`). Rationale: same-named tables across product schemas (`customers` ×3, `employees` ×2, `categories` ×2) make a global multi-schema `search_path` impossible. Search Projections per-product (`chinook.search_projections`, etc.); drops atomically with `DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE` during Product Reset — aligns with #7 atomic-per-product. Source Identity Registry, Reset Run, Pin Manifest, and the shared `en_unaccent` text search config live in `public` so they survive per-product reset. Federated Search uses `UNION ALL` across the three product schemas with literal `product_tenant` labels. Migrations organised per-product (`database/migrations/{chinook,northwind,sakila}/`). #7's stale "SQLite single-writer" Reset Window rationale retired (Postgres is MVCC); Reset Window behaviour unchanged. Unblocks #32 (column shape) and #42 (extension lifecycle).
- [Postgres extension management selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) — Single early migration `0001_01_01_000000_create_postgres_extensions.php` declares `vector`, `unaccent`, `pg_trgm` extensions + `en_unaccent` text search config via `DB::statement('CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS …')` on the default `pgsql` connection. `down()` is a no-op (extensions are infrastructure; rolling back must not cascade-drop data). No version pin in DDL (Herd-bundled policy from #40). No `pgsql::direct` for now (default connection sufficient for Herd + CI; swappable if pooler enters). CI: `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` Docker service container. Verification: Pest test `test_postgres_extensions_are_installed` (gates every CI build), `php artisan pgsql:check` command (deploy-time operator check), README docs (Herd Pro prerequisite). All 14 SQLite-specific terms from #12 fully dissolve; none transform. Supersedes #12; closes the Postgres-pivot trio (#40+#41+#42). DB tier is now fully charted for execution.
- [Search Projection column shape selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/32) — Per-product `*.search_projections` table: UUIDv7 Domain Identity as PK directly (integer `search_id` bridge from #8 dissolves — pgvector has no integer-PK requirement); four weight-class text columns (`weight_d/c/b/a_text`) written by Postgres trigger from the source entity's Search Document fields (#31 owns the per-entity mapping); `document_tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (setweight(to_tsvector('en_unaccent', …), 'D') || …) STORED` materialises #40's ABCD weighting in-storage (PG18 canonical pattern, transactionally current by construction); `embedding vector(1536)` + `embedding_profile` + `content_digest` + `embedded_at` + `embedding_state` (`pending`/`complete`/`failed`/`mismatched`/`lexical_only`) for the semantic side; tier-2 rows live in the same table with NULL embedding (`lexical_only` state, HNSW skips them automatically). Integrity: Postgres trigger (authoritative content writer + state reset) + Eloquent observer (queues embedding job post-commit). After-commit verification transforms — drops defensive re-check (ACID covers it), adds Baseline Invariant `embedding_state NOT IN ('complete','lexical_only')` count = 0 at end of Product Import/Reset. HNSW (`m=16`, `ef_construction=64`, `ef_search=40`) + GIN (`fastupdate=on`) defaults confirmed. Refines #8 (search_id retires, after-commit rationale becomes operational not correctness), #41 (concrete shape for the per-product projection tables), #7 (new publish-gate Baseline Invariant). Unblocks #33 (Embedding Profile impl — target columns fixed) and #34 (RRF + Federated Search — query targets fixed).
- [Search Document shape per entity selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/31) — Tier assignments: 11 tier-1 (hybrid — Chinook Artist/Album/Track/Playlist, Northwind Product/Category/Supplier, Sakila Film/Actor/Category/Language), 13 tier-2 (lexical-only — Chinook Customer/Employee/Invoice/Genre, Northwind Customer/Employee/Order/Shipper, Sakila Customer/Staff/Rental/Payment/Store; operator override placed Staff/Payment/Store as tier 2 despite auth-credential and money-sensitivity concerns), ~16 tier-3 (excluded — all join tables, contact/location tables, internal-org tables, `film_text`, `media_types`). Tier-1 field→weight mapping pinned per entity per #40's ABCD scheme: weight_d = title/name, weight_c = description (Track.Composer, Product.QuantityPerUnit, Film.Description, Category.Description), weight_b = category (Track→Genre.Name via FK subquery, Product→Category.CategoryName via FK subquery, Film→Category.name via film_category join + Rating), weight_a = `source_id` (universal). FK→Name resolution via subquery inside the PL/pgSQL trigger function (no denormalised columns on source tables). Search Surface exclusives consolidated: contact data, location data, money (`*_minor`), Blob Assets, auth credentials (`Staff.username`/`password`), relationship-only rows, internal metadata, pre-computed search columns. `entity_type` discriminator = singular snake_case (Eloquent morph type convention); product identity carried by schema name per #41 (federated query adds literal `product_tenant` label). Produces the complete CASE mapping table for #32's trigger execution. Closes the wayfinder-level search cluster — #33/#34 are implementation tickets, no further wayfinder decisions required.
- [Upstream datasets re-verified — zero drift](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/27) — All three sources (Chinook `lerocha/chinook-database` @ `7f67772`, Northwind `jpwhite3/northwind-SQLite3` @ `4f56e7f`, Sakila `bradleygrant/sakila-sqlite3` @ `9394b42`) re-verified 2026-07-21 against live sources with freshly recomputed SHA-256 digests; every pinned commit is still HEAD of its default branch, every digest matches #4 byte-for-byte, no mirror moved or archived. One non-material note for #28: Chinook's `v1.4.5` *tag* is not byte-equivalent to the pinned commit (CRLF→LF normalization) — importer must resolve by commit SHA, never by tag. Pin Manifest still lives only in the #4 audit doc; materialising it into the repo is #28/T4.1's job. Unblocks #28 (Product Import pipeline).
- [Filament 5 + Livewire teams starter co-install verified](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/19) — Co-install is viable on the shared `web` guard; Shield v4 carries the Filament 5 compatibility badge. No guard collision, no route collision (Fortify `/login` and Filament `/admin/login` are in disjoint URI trees). Four decision forks surfaced — these are the spine of #16 and #26: (1) **2FA ownership** — Fortify's `TwoFactorAuthenticatable` vs Filament v5's built-in MFA, one must own the challenge flow; (2) **panel scope + tenancy** — `/admin` as global cross-team panel vs Filament tenancy with `Team` as tenant (the starter's `EnsureTeamMembership` reads a `{current_team}` route param panel routes don't carry, so it cannot gate `/admin` as-is); (3) **dual role systems** — Shield's global spatie roles vs the starter's team-scoped `TeamRole`/`TeamPermission` enums, need an explicit mapping policy; (4) **policy-directory convention** — Shield writes to `app/Policies/` and would target the existing `TeamPolicy` if a `TeamResource` is added. One open uncertainty flagged for #26: no official Filament v5 + Fortify coexistence recipe exists — the "reuse Fortify session, disable Filament auth" path is inferred from guest-access docs, not blessed. Unblocks #16 and #26.
- [UUIDv7 implementation strategy selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/24) — Laravel 13's native `HasUuids` trait generates UUIDv7 by default (verified against 13.x Eloquent docs; `ramsey/uuid` 4.9.3 + `symfony/uid` 8.1.0 already present). No package, no custom generator, no `newUniqueId()` override. **Six decisions:** (1) **native generation + registry reuse** over deterministic derivation — #25's existence implies it is the identity-continuity mechanism (content-hash derivation would make the registry redundant and forfeit v7 index locality); (2) **Postgres native `uuid` column** (`$table->uuid('id')`, no `AsBinary` cast — that's for DBs lacking native uuid); (3) **rewrite the starter migrations in place** (`users` + `teams` + join tables: `id()`→`uuid('id')`, `foreignId()`→`foreignUuid()`) — pre-data, `0001_01_01_…` designed to be edited, repo bootstrapped *from* not forked *of* the starter; (4) **per-model `use HasUuids;`** — trait sets `$incrementing`/`$keyType` internally so it's one line per model, consistent with #41's per-model `#[Table]` attribute, no shared base class (YAGNI); (5) **UUIDv7 PK on every app-owned table** — `users`, `teams`, `team_members`, `team_invitations` (operator override — moved in for consistency: no bigInteger PKs anywhere in app-owned tables), all product-domain tables, shared `public` domain tables; framework-standard keys kept only on pure Laravel infra (`password_reset_tokens`, `sessions`, `jobs`, `failed_jobs`, `job_batches`, `cache`, `cache_locks`, `migrations`); (6) **import hook = explicit-id-on-reuse** — importer sets `$model->id` from the registry on a hit (bypassing `HasUuids`), leaves it unset on a miss so the trait generates, then records the mapping. Overriding `newUniqueId()` rejected (couples models to registry, needs source-context only the importer has). Unblocks #25 (registry shape now the only open identity question) and #28 (with #27).
- [Source Identity Registry selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/25) — One shared `public.source_identities` table for all three products; survives `DROP SCHEMA <product> CASCADE` by location (per #41). **Eight decisions:** (1) **single shared table** in `public`, not three per-product tables; (2) **JSONB `source_key`** for atomic (`{"id":"5"}`) and composite (`{"order_id":"10248","product_id":"11"}`) source identities, all components as strings per #6; (3) **`entity` discriminator = schema-qualified table name** (`chinook.artists`, etc.) — globally unique per #41, decoupled from PHP class locations; (4) **`product` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (split_part(entity,'.',1)) STORED`** — derived, materialised, drift-proof; (5) **lifecycle columns = `created_at`/`updated_at` only** — no FKs to `reset_runs` (wrong shape: first import isn't a Reset Run) or `pin_manifests` (premature; cheap `ALTER TABLE` later); (6) **no FK in either direction with product tables, `reset_runs`, or `pin_manifests`** — registry is fully self-contained, `domain_id` is a copy not a reference; (7) **registry writes are OUTSIDE the reset transaction, immediate autocommit** — required for identity stability across failed-and-retried resets (the same source row mints the same UUID on every attempt); harmless stale mappings tolerated for UUIDs minted but never materialised; (8) **monotonic append-mostly, no GC** — mappings are immutable once written; absence observable via `updated_at < current_import_started_at`, not stored state. `UNIQUE (entity, source_key)`; CHECK regex `^(chinook|northwind|sakila)\.[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` on `entity`. Migration: `database/migrations/0001_01_01_000001_create_source_identities_table.php` (root, not product subdir). Realises #24's explicit-id-on-reuse contract; refines #41 and #7; unblocks #28 (Product Import pipeline — lookup/mint contract fixed) and refines #29 (Reset semantics — step 4 registry interaction specified).
- [Filament 5 panel install order and discovery-root pattern selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/16) — Four panels installed up-front in a 14-step sequence (Filament → configure Admin → make+configure ×3 products → Shield → publish config → HasRoles+FilamentUser+canAccessPanel on User → shield:setup → shield:generate --panel=admin → baseline-operator migration → update DatabaseSeeder → update Vite/Tailwind). Five sub-decisions: (1) **global panels, no Filament tenancy** — no `->tenant(Team::class)`, no `EnsureTeamMembership` in any panel; grounded in CONTEXT.md's anti-tenant glossary ("Avoid: tenant" ×2, "Team Owner has no authority over shared sample data", "Global Role Administration does not manage Team Ownership"); dissolves #19 fork 5 (Team schema mismatch) for #26; (2) **Fortify owns all auth, Filament login disabled on all four panels** — all `PanelProvider`s omit `->login()`/`->registration()`/`->passwordReset()`/`->emailVerification()`, keep `Authenticate::class`; starter's `LoginResponse` already uses `redirect()->intended($fallback)` so post-auth bounce-back to `/admin` works free (no code change); Filament's built-in MFA NOT enabled (Fortify's 2FA is the only MFA surface); `FilamentUser::canAccessPanel` is the per-panel gate; dissolves #19 fork 1 (2FA ownership) for #26; (3) **baseline-operator migration** — env-driven creds (`OPERATOR_EMAIL`/`OPERATOR_PASSWORD`/`OPERATOR_NAME` from `.env`, dev defaults in `.env.example`), personal team via `CreateTeam` action (name `"System Operator's Team"`, slug `system-operator-s-team` — no `/admin` route collision), `super_admin` Shield role, idempotent (`firstOrCreate`), no-op `down()`; sequenced after Shield's role migration; `DatabaseSeeder` drops bare `Test User` (starter bug — no team, instant 403); production operator-onboarding deferred to #26; (4) **per-panel discovery roots** — each panel discovers only `App\Filament\<Product>/{Resources,Pages,Widgets}` via explicit `->discoverResources/Pages/Widgets` calls; default shared discovery removed from every panel; no clusters; Livewire SFC app UI registers via `routes/web.php`, not panel discovery; (5) **Shield in Admin only** — `FilamentShieldPlugin::make()` in `AdminPanelProvider` only; `shield:generate --panel=admin` only; product panels use `canAccessPanel` + hand-written policies (not Shield-generated); product-scoped roles (`chinook_curator`/`northwind_curator`/`sakila_curator`/`super_admin`) are global Spatie roles managed via Admin's `RoleResource` (Shield plugin = role-management UI + policy generator; Spatie's `HasRoles` works anywhere regardless of plugin registration). Panel IDs/paths permanent: `admin`/`/admin`, `chinook`/`/chinook`, `northwind`/`/northwind`, `sakila`/`/sakila`. `canAccessPanel` pattern: `match($panel->getId())` → admin checks `hasRole('super_admin')`; products check `hasRole("{$panel->getId()}_curator")` OR `hasRole('super_admin')`; role names fixed here as the contract between #16 and #26, contents/assignment/glossary-refinement deferred to #26. Unblocks #30 (Resource generation — discovery roots fixed); refines #17 (test pyramid — Authorization Acceptance Matrix test shapes needed for `canAccessPanel` × panel × role); refines #26 (refined spine — forks 1 and 5 dissolved, seven specific inputs graduated).
- [Test pyramid decided](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/17) — **Dual-suite Pest 4 pyramid**: four MANDATORY PR-gated layers (Unit, Feature, Architecture, Livewire-component); Browser/Dusk OUT OF SCOPE for Stage 1 (re-evaluate at Stage 5+); Mutation, 100 % line coverage, 100 % type-coverage, Larastan max+no-baseline, `carthage-software/mago` arch depth, `rector/rector` lint depth all ASPIRATIONAL (visible per-PR, never blocking). **Dual test DB**: default `tests/Feature/*` on SQLite `:memory:` for non-PG tests;
